key_insight: AI, especially deep learning, is making weld inspection faster, more consistent, and more objective by learning from digital non-destructive testing data.
engineering_relevance: This work matters for manufacturing, energy, transportation, and shipbuilding because reliable weld quality directly affects structural safety and long-term durability.
method: Systematic review of recent AI-based weld quality control literature
Compared machine learning, CNNs, object detection/segmentation, transfer learning, and hybrid frameworks
Examined non-destructive testing modalities, defect types, and real-time monitoring use cases
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that recent deep learning models achieve high defect detection, classification, segmentation, and quality-prediction performance across multiple NDT data sources.
watch_item: Industrial deployment is still constrained by limited and imbalanced datasets, domain shift, weak generalization, and the need for explainable, standards-compliant AI.
paper_title: Artificial Intelligence in Quality Control of Welded Joints
